area.title: Notification lists: cards, tabs, search, sort and filters
area.scope: A category's notifications list (DR2.1 live animals and germinal products lists; today's animals dashboard): summary cards, tabs, notification cards and the facts and statuses they show, the actions a card offers, search, sort, additional filters, pagination, results count, empty and success states, and the list APIs and read model behind them (animals backend list, INS backend read model). Stops at what each card action does (manage-notifications). Includes the high-risk plants frontend's dashboard (its notification list), its cards, sort, search, pagination, row actions, late tag and its dashboard rulings, since plants' list is reframed in the same increments.

sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled; the real persistence and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express

claims.statement: The service keeps one summary document per notification in a MongoDB collection named notifications.
claims.quote: @Document(collection = "notifications")

claims.statement: The notifications collection lives in the MongoDB database named by MONGO_DATABASE, default trade-imports-ins-backend.
claims.quote: database: ${MONGO_DATABASE:trade-imports-ins-backend}

claims.statement: The document's id is aggregateId, a string, taken from the event body's aggregateId and set only when the document is first inserted.
claims.quote:
@Id
    private String aggregateId; ... .setOnInsert("_id", aggregateId)

claims.statement: aggregateVersion is a whole number (long) taken from the event body's aggregateVersion and set on every applied event.
claims.quote: private long aggregateVersion; ... .set(AGGREGATE_VERSION, incomingVersion)

claims.statement: referenceNumber is a string taken from data.exchangedDocument.identifier in the event, such as GBN-AG-26-001.
claims.quote: String referenceNumber = text(exchangedDocument.path("identifier"));

claims.statement: organisationId is a string taken from the top-level organisationId of the event body, and it is set on every applied event.
claims.quote: String organisationId = text(body.path(ORGANISATION_ID)); ... update.set(ORGANISATION_ID, organisationId);

claims.statement: status is a free string copied as-is from data.exchangedDocument.notificationStatusCode. The read model does not derive, map or validate the status value.
claims.quote: String status = text(exchangedDocument.path("notificationStatusCode"));
claims.note: The type is String, not an enum, so any value the publisher sends is stored.

claims.statement: The status values the slice shows are DRAFT and SUBMITTED, which the tests send as notificationStatusCode and read back from the stored document.
claims.quote: assertThat(doc.get().getStatus()).isEqualTo("DRAFT"); ... .hasValue("SUBMITTED"));

claims.statement: The slice holds no list of the status values the read model accepts or expects: no enum, schema or doc enumerates them, and the event schema is not defined in this repo.
claims.quote: the schema itself is not defined in this repo.
claims.note: Looked in AggregatedNotification, NotificationUpsertService, OutboxEventType, README, AGENTS.md, docs/architecture.md and the workspace page.

claims.statement: The workspace repo page says notifications with status DELETED are excluded from what the read API returns, so DELETED is a status value the model expects to hold.
claims.quote: Notifications with status `DELETED` are excluded.
claims.note: The exclusion itself is in the query API, part 2. Nothing on the ingest side sets DELETED: it would arrive as notificationStatusCode.

claims.statement: originCountry is a string code taken from data.specifiedConsignment.originCountry.code.value, such as GB or ES.
claims.quote: String originCountry = text(originCountryNode.path("code").path("value"));

claims.statement: originCountrySubdivisionCode is the identifier of the origin country's sub-division whose functionTypeCode content is 106, the UNCL3227 'Region of origin' function, such as ES-CN.
claims.quote: private static final String LOCATION_FUNCTION_SUBDIVISION_OF_ORIGIN = "106";

claims.statement: The subdivision is picked by its function code 106, not by its position in the sub-division list, so a country carrying other sub-divisions first still stores the function-106 one.
claims.quote: A country can carry other sub-divisions too, so the code is picked by its function, not its position.

claims.statement: The read model does not store the event's regionOfOriginCode.
claims.quote: INS uses it for the country subdivision the goods came from, and does not store a region of origin code.

claims.statement: An event that carries an origin country but no function-106 subdivision clears any stored originCountrySubdivisionCode.
claims.quote: An event that carries an origin with no subdivision, such as an amendment from the Canary Islands to mainland France, clears it.

claims.statement: An event with no origin country, such as a lifecycle event, leaves the stored originCountrySubdivisionCode alone.
claims.quote: An event with no origin at all, such as a lifecycle event, leaves it alone.

claims.statement: commodity is a string taken from the first trade line of the first consignment item: its first description entry.
claims.quote: String commodity = text(firstTradeLine.path("description").path(0));

claims.statement: When the first trade line has no description, commodity falls back to that trade line's commonName, and the service logs the aggregate id and version when it does.
claims.quote: The dashboard `commodity` field is the first trade line's `description`, or `commonName` when description is absent. A log line records aggregate id and version when the commonName fallback is used.

claims.statement: Only the first trade line is read for commodity, so a notification with several commodity lines shows one commodity in the read model.
claims.quote:
.path("includedConsignmentItem").path(0)
            .path("includedTradeLineItem").path(0);
claims.note: mechanism: reduces the event's trade lines to one commodity string. Inferred from index 0 being the only element read.

claims.statement: arrivalDate is a calendar date taken from the first transport movement's first arrival event's scheduledOccurrenceDateTime, an instant, reduced to its calendar day in UTC.
claims.quote: .atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate()

claims.statement: The arrival day is taken back in UTC whatever the server's time zone, because the animals backend writes the arrival at the start of the chosen day in UTC and PIMS needs an instant.
claims.quote: The GBN-AG event carries the arrival as an instant, `scheduledOccurrenceDateTime`, because PIMS needs one. The animals backend writes it at the start of the chosen day in UTC, so `NotificationUpsertService` takes the day back in UTC, whatever the JVM's zone.

claims.statement: arrivalDate is stored in Mongo as a YYYY-MM-DD string, not a BSON date, and read back as a calendar date.
claims.quote: `arrivalDate` is a calendar date: a `LocalDate` on the document and in the API, `YYYY-MM-DD` on the wire, and a string in Mongo.

claims.statement: arrivalDate is stored as a string so the stored day does not depend on where the service runs, and because YYYY-MM-DD strings sort in date order the arrivalDate sort and the compound index work on the string.
claims.quote: Without them Spring Data writes a BSON date at midnight in the JVM's zone, and the stored day then depends on where the service runs. `YYYY-MM-DD` strings sort in date order, so the `arrivalDate` sort and the `organisation_status_sort_fields` index work on the string.

claims.statement: lastUpdated is a moment in time taken from data.exchangedDocument.issueDateTime and stored as a BSON date.
claims.quote: `lastUpdated` is a moment: an `Instant`, RFC 3339 with a `Z` on the wire, and a BSON date in Mongo.

claims.statement: When an event has no issueDateTime, lastUpdated is set to the time the service processes the event.
claims.note: mechanism: lastUpdated falls back to processing time.

claims.statement: The document has exactly 10 fields: aggregateId, aggregateVersion, referenceNumber, organisationId, status, originCountry, originCountrySubdivisionCode, commodity, arrivalDate and lastUpdated. It holds no notification category, no journey or set, no port, no consignor or importer, and no commodity code.
claims.note: The absence of other fields is read from the class having only these. The commodity classCode the test events carry (01059900) is not stored.

claims.statement: A field the event does not carry, or carries blank or not as text, is left as it is stored rather than cleared; only aggregateVersion, lastUpdated and organisationId are written on every applied event.
claims.quote:
if (referenceNumber != null) update.set("referenceNumber", referenceNumber);
        if (status != null) update.set("status", status);
claims.note: mechanism: partial update of the stored summary. originCountrySubdivisionCode is the exception, cleared when an origin arrives without one.

claims.statement: Each event is applied in one atomic Mongo upsert whose query matches the document's id and a stored aggregateVersion lower than the incoming one, so concurrent and out-of-order events converge on the highest version with no read-then-write race.
claims.quote: `NotificationUpsertService` writes each event in one Mongo upsert whose query matches only a stored `aggregateVersion` lower than the incoming one. Concurrent events for the same notification and out-of-order redelivery both converge on the highest version, with no read-then-write race.

claims.statement: An event for a notification not yet stored inserts a new document.
claims.quote: mongoTemplate.upsert(query, update, AggregatedNotification.class);

claims.statement: An event whose aggregateVersion is equal to or lower than the stored one changes nothing: the service does not skip it itself but leaves it to the version filter.
claims.quote: upsert_shouldLeaveStaleEventsToTheVersionFilter_ratherThanSkippingThemItself

claims.statement: A stale or duplicate event for an existing document misses the version filter, so the upsert tries to insert a second document with the same id; that failure is unclassified, so the message is treated as non-retryable and deleted.
claims.quote:
Criteria.where("_id").is(aggregateId)
                .and(AGGREGATE_VERSION).lt(incomingVersion));
claims.note: mechanism: Mongo upsert semantics. Inferred from an upsert whose query misses while _id is fixed by setOnInsert; the duplicate-key error is caught by the error handler as unclassified. The tests prove only the outcome (document unchanged, queue drained), and each such message is counted as discarded and logged at error.

claims.statement: An event body with a missing or blank aggregateId is rejected as non-retryable.
claims.quote: throw new SqsNonRetryableException("Missing aggregateId in event body");

claims.statement: An event body with a missing or negative aggregateVersion is rejected as non-retryable.
claims.quote: throw new SqsNonRetryableException("Missing or negative aggregateVersion in event body for aggregateId=" + aggregateId);

claims.statement: An event body with a missing or blank organisationId is rejected as non-retryable, so every stored notification belongs to an organisation.
claims.quote:
throw new SqsNonRetryableException(
                "Missing " + ORGANISATION_ID + " in event body for aggregateId=" + aggregateId);

claims.statement: An issueDateTime that is not an ISO instant is rejected as non-retryable.
claims.quote:
throw new SqsNonRetryableException(
                "Invalid " + fieldName + " for aggregateId=" + aggregateId, e);

claims.statement: A scheduledOccurrenceDateTime that is not a full instant, such as a bare date 2026-07-21, is rejected as non-retryable.
claims.quote: upsert_shouldRejectAsNonRetryable_whenScheduledOccurrenceDateTimeHasNoTime

claims.statement: A lifecycle event with no data payload still updates aggregateVersion, lastUpdated and organisationId, and leaves every other stored field as it was.
claims.quote: upsert_shouldSetVersionLastUpdatedAndOrganisation_whenLifecycleEventHasNoData

claims.statement: The service reads notification events from an SQS FIFO queue whose URL is set by NOTIFICATION_SQS_QUEUE_URL.
claims.quote: @SqsListener("${aws.sqs.notification.queue-url}")

claims.statement: The queue is trade_imports_animals_eu_notifications_ins_backend.fifo, subscribed with raw message delivery to the SNS FIFO topic trade_imports_animals_eu_notifications.fifo, to which trade-imports-animals-backend publishes its outbox events.
claims.quote: SNS FIFO topic `trade_imports_animals_eu_notifications.fifo`, subscribed to the queue with raw message delivery | SNS to SQS | Fan-out. trade-imports-animals-backend publishes its outbox events to this topic

claims.statement: Only the animals backend publishes to the read model's queue today, so the read model holds animals notifications only; no plants source feeds it.
claims.quote: trade-imports-animals-backend publishes its outbox events to this topic
claims.note: Inferred from the only named publisher and queue name (animals_eu_notifications). The slice names no plants topic or queue.

claims.statement: The event body is a GBN-AG structure with exchangedDocument and specifiedConsignment under data; its schema is not defined in this repo.
claims.quote: The message body uses an `exchangedDocument` / `specifiedConsignment` structure (fields such as `notificationStatusCode`, `issueDateTime`, `originCountry`); the schema itself is not defined in this repo.

claims.statement: A message with a missing or blank FIFO message group id is rejected as non-retryable; the message group id is the notification's aggregate id.
claims.quote: throw new SqsNonRetryableException("Missing or blank MESSAGE_GROUP_ID: " + aggregateId);

claims.statement: The listener does not check that the message group id matches the aggregateId in the body: the stored document's id comes from the body.
claims.quote: String aggregateId = body.path("aggregateId").asText(null);
claims.note: Inferred from the listener passing only the parsed body to the upsert.

claims.statement: A message with an empty or missing body is rejected as non-retryable.
claims.quote: throw new SqsNonRetryableException("Empty message body for aggregateId=" + aggregateId);

claims.statement: A message body that is not valid JSON is rejected as non-retryable.
claims.quote: throw new SqsNonRetryableException("Message body is not valid JSON for aggregateId=" + aggregateId, e);

claims.statement: A message whose eventType is not one of the recognised event types is logged at error and rejected as non-retryable rather than silently acknowledged.
claims.quote: log.error("Unrecognised eventType={} aggregateId={} — dead-lettering", eventType, aggregateId);

claims.statement: The recognised event types are eight wire values under uk.gov.defra.imports.notification: NotificationEdited, NotificationSubmitted, NotificationSubmissionAmended, NotificationCreated, NotificationAmendmentRequested, NotificationAmendmentCancelled, NotificationDeleted and NotificationSubmissionDeleted.
claims.quote:
NOTIFICATION_EDITED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationEdited"),
    NOTIFICATION_SUBMITTED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationSubmitted"),
    NOTIFICATION_SUBMISSION_AMENDED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationSubmissionAmended"),
    NOTIFICATION_CREATED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationCreated"),
    NOTIFICATION_AMENDMENT_REQUESTED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationAmendmentRequested"),
    NOTIFICATION_AMENDMENT_CANCELLED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationAmendmentCancelled"),
    NOTIFICATION_DELETED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationDeleted"),
    NOTIFICATION_SUBMISSION_DELETED("uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.NotificationSubmissionDeleted");

claims.statement: Every recognised event type does the same thing to the read model: the whole body goes through the one upsert. No event type is special-cased.
claims.quote:
log.debug("Processing eventType={} aggregateId={}", resolved, aggregateId);
        upsertService.upsert(parsedBody);

claims.statement: NotificationDeleted and NotificationSubmissionDeleted events do not remove the document from the read model; the document stays and takes whatever status and fields the event carries.
claims.quote: upsertService.upsert(parsedBody);
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any remove for these event types; the only remove is the start-up clean-up of documents without organisationId.

claims.statement: Each processed and upserted message increments the metric notification.ins.sqs.messages with outcome processed.
claims.quote:
Counter.builder("notification.ins.sqs.messages")
            .tag("outcome", "processed")

claims.statement: Every received message is logged at info with its aggregate id, receive count and body length, not its body.
claims.quote: log.info("Received notification event: aggregateId={}, receiveCount={}, bodyLength={}",

claims.statement: An error classified as retryable leaves the message on the queue for SQS to redeliver, increments notification.ins.sqs.errors with action retry and logs at warn with the aggregate id and message id.
claims.quote: log.warn("Retryable error, message left for retry: aggregateId={}, messageId={}",

claims.statement: An error classified as non-retryable deletes the message, increments notification.ins.sqs.errors with action discarded and logs at error with the aggregate id, message id and the error.
claims.quote: log.error("Non-retryable error, message will be deleted: aggregateId={}, messageId={}",

claims.statement: The error handler classifies an error by the first retryable or non-retryable error it finds down the cause chain, and treats any error with neither as non-retryable, so the message is deleted.
claims.quote:
if (current instanceof SqsRetryableException || current instanceof SqsNonRetryableException) {
                return current;

claims.statement: Nothing on the ingest path raises a retryable error, so a transient failure such as Mongo being unavailable is treated as non-retryable and the event is deleted rather than retried.
claims.quote:
discardedCounter.increment();
        log.error("Non-retryable error, message will be deleted: aggregateId={}, messageId={}",
claims.note: Inferred: SqsRetryableException is defined but no file in the slice throws it. A lost event leaves the read model behind its source until a later event for the same notification arrives.

claims.statement: A rejected message is deleted, not moved to a dead-letter queue: no dead-letter queue is configured in this slice, although the log and the workspace page call it dead-lettering.
claims.quote: Retry versus dead-letter classification of bad messages (`SqsRetryableException`, `SqsNonRetryableException`).
claims.note: The queue's own redrive policy, if any, would be in floci/setup-ins-backend-pipeline.sh or CDP config, neither in this slice.

claims.statement: The SQS long-poll wait time is set by SQS_WAIT_TIME_SECONDS, default 10, and must be between 0 and 20 seconds.
claims.quote: @Min(0) @Max(20) int waitTimeSeconds,

claims.statement: The maximum number of SQS messages is set by SQS_MAX_MESSAGES, default 10, and must be between 1 and 10.
claims.quote: @Min(1) @Max(10) int maxMessages) {

claims.statement: The notification queue URL must not be blank.
claims.quote: @NotBlank String queueUrl,

claims.statement: The notifications collection has a compound index named organisation_status_sort_fields on organisationId ascending, status ascending, arrivalDate descending and lastUpdated descending.
claims.quote: def = "{'organisationId': 1, 'status': 1, 'arrivalDate': -1, 'lastUpdated': -1}")

claims.statement: The notifications collection has a single-field index on referenceNumber.
claims.quote:
@Indexed
    private String referenceNumber;

claims.statement: Indexes are created automatically when the service starts.
claims.quote: auto-index-creation: true

claims.statement: No index covers originCountry, commodity or originCountrySubdivisionCode.
claims.quote:
@CompoundIndex(
    name = AggregatedNotification.ORGANISATION_STATUS_SORT_INDEX,
claims.note: Inferred from the only two index declarations on the class. Filtering or sorting by these fields would need a new index.

claims.statement: At start-up the service drops the legacy status_sort_fields index if it exists, so existing databases take the new index without a manual step, and carries on starting if there is none to drop.
claims.quote:
